questions.question: Under the Koppen climate classification system, which climate zone is generally located on the western coasts of continents, receiving rainfall between 35-90 cm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mediterranean Climate.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mediterranean climate zone** is characterized by** mild, wet winters** and** hot, dry summers.**
 
• This climate zone is typically located on the western coasts of continents, including regions such as **California, the Mediterranean Basin**, and parts of **Australia and South Africa.**
 
• The **35-90 cm of rainfall **received in this **climate zone** is typically concentrated in the winter months.
 
• Other characteristics of this climate zone include vegetation such as **chaparral, sclerophyll forests, and cork oak** forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Humid Subtropical climate zone** is characterized by hot, humid summers and mild winters.

 
 
• It is typically found in regions such as the southeastern** United States, eastern China**, and parts of **South America**.
 
 
 
• The **Subtropical Steppe climate zone** is characterized by hot, dry summers and mild winters.
 
 
• It is typically found in regions such as the **Great Plains of the United States**, parts of** Australia, and southern Africa.**
 
 
 
• The **Highland climate zone** is characterized by **cooler temperatures **at higher elevations.
 
 
• It can include a variety of sub-climates such as** alpine, tundra, and boreal forests.**

questions.question: The following represent the opportunity cost of holding money, EXCEPT:

options.text: loss of utility from goods that could have been purchased from the same amount of money
loss of interest earning on cash holdings
loss of purchasing power of money due to inflation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** transaction cost in withdrawing money.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Opportunity cost** is the cost of the next best alternative forgone in order to pursue a **certain action.**
 
• **Holding money** also has an opportunity cost, which is the** loss of potential benefits **that could have been obtained by using that money for something else.
 
• Transaction costs are the expenses incurred in **buying or selling goods or services** and are **not** related to the opportunity cost of holding money.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Loss of utility from goods that could have been purchased **with the same amount of money is a common opportunity cost of holding money.

 
 
• This is because money can only provide** utility** when it is used to purchase goods or services that satisfy a need or want.
 
 
 
• **Loss of interest-earning on cash holdings** is another opportunity cost of holding money.
 
 
• This is because money that is held in cash **does not** generate any returns, unlike money that is invested in stocks, bonds, or other financial instruments.
 
 
 
• **Loss of purchasing power of money due to inflation** is also a significant opportunity cost of holding money.
 
 
• Inflation reduces the value of **money over time**, making it less valuable in terms of the goods and services it can purchase.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for excessive cold in north India?

options.text: Cold winds from the Caspian Sea

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equatorial current.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• Equatorial current is **not a reason** for excessive cold in north India.
 
• It is a **warm ocean current** that flows towards the west and affects the **climate of regions** near the equator.
 
• The **Himalayas** are the highest mountain range in the world and play a significant role in shaping the climate of north India.
 
• The region is also influenced by the **monsoon winds** that bring rainfall during the summer months.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Distance from the sea **is a reason for excessive cold in north India because the absence of a** moderating influence of the sea** makes the winters harsh and the summers hot.
 
• **Cold winds from the Caspian Sea** are a reason for excessive cold in north India because they** bring dry and cold air **to the region and cause a drop in temperature.
 
• **Snowfall in the Himalayas** is a reason for excessive cold in north India because it leads to the formation of **glaciers and snow cover** that reflect sunlight and reduce the amount of heat absorbed by the ground.

questions.question: The threshold limit for total income eligible for rebate under Section 87A has been increased from ₹5,00,000 to ₹______ for assesses opting for the new tax regime as per the Finance Bill 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7,00,000.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Bill 2023** has proposed an increase in the threshold limit for total income eligible for rebate under **Section 87A **for assesses who opt for the new tax regime.
 
• Section 87A provides a rebate of up to** Rs.12,500** to taxpayers whose total income does not exceed a certain limit.
 
• This limit has been increased from **Rs. 5,00,000 to Rs. 7,00,000 **for assesses opting for the new tax regime.
 
• The new tax regime was introduced in the Union Budget 2020 and offers lower tax rates to taxpayers who forego certain deductions and exemptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The tax rates under the new regime are as follows:
 
 
• For income up to **Rs**. **2.5 lakhs: Nil**
 
• For income between **Rs. 2.5 lakhs and Rs. 5 lakhs: 5%**
 
• For income between** Rs. 5 lakhs and Rs. 7.5 lakhs: 10%**
 
• For income between **Rs. 7.5 lakhs and Rs. 10 lakhs: 15%**
 
• For income between** Rs. 10 lakhs and Rs. 12.5 lakhs: 20%**
 
• For income between** Rs. 12.5 lakhs and Rs. 15 lakhs: 25%**
 
• For income above **Rs. 15 lakhs: 30%**
 
 
 
• **11,00,000 **is the threshold limit for availing the **standard deduction** for salaried individuals.
 
• The standard deduction is a** fixed deduction **allowed to salaried individuals in lieu of certain expenses such as conveyance, medical expenses, etc.
 
• **8,00,000** is the threshold limit for **senior citizens** to avail of tax exemption on interest income from deposits with banks, post offices, and cooperative banks.
 
• **10,00,000** is the threshold limit for tax exemption on** long-term capital gains** arising from the sale of equity shares or equity-oriented mutual funds.

questions.question: Which of the following Commissions was appointed by Lord Curzon to enquire into the working of the police administration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frazer Commission.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Frazer Commission **was appointed by **Lord Curzon in 1902 **to enquire into the workings of the **police administration **in British India.
 
• The commission was headed by **Sir James Frazer**, a retired judge of the** Calcutta High Court**, and had six other members.
 
• The commission submitted its report in **1903,** which recommended several **reforms in the police system**, including the separation of investigation and law and order functions, the establishment of a central training institution, and the improvement of working conditions for police personnel.
 
• The recommendations of the Frazer Commission were implemented in various parts of British India and laid the foundation for the** modern police system in India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Kitchener Commission **was appointed in **1913.**

 
 
• It was made to enquire into the **military system of British India** and recommend reforms.
 
 
 
• The** Hunter Commission** was appointed in **1919.**
 
 
• Its goal was to enquire into the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** and the** Punjab disturbances** of **1919.**
 
 
 
• The **MacDonnell Commission** was appointed in **1924.**
 
 
• Its aim was to enquire into the communal riots in** Kohat and Peshawar** in the North-West Frontier Province of British India.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: There is a legal sanction against their violation.
They are part of the Indian tradition.
They are not sacrosanct or permanent.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** There is a legal sanction against their violation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution **do not **have a **legal sanction** against their violation.
 
• They are **non-enforceable** in nature.
 
• Fundamental duties are a part of the** Indian tradition**, as they reflect the values and principles that have been upheld by Indian society for centuries.
 
• Through the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976,** the essential responsibilities of citizens were enumerated in this constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental duties are **indeed civic duties **that citizens are expected to perform.

 
 
• These duties include respecting the** national flag **and the **Constitution**, protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, promoting harmony and brotherhood among all people, etc.
 
 
 
• Fundamental duties are based on** Indian tradition and culture.** 
 
 
• They reflect the** values and principles** that have been upheld by Indian society for centuries.
 
 
 
• Fundamental duties are **not sacrosanct or permanent.** 
 
 
• They can be **amended or repealed** by the Parliament if necessary.

questions.question: Under the current regulatory framework, what is the maximum tenure of a microfinance loan in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**36 months.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** maximum tenure** of a microfinance loan in India under the current regulatory framework is **36 months**, which means a borrower can take a loan for up to** 3 years.**
 
• Microfinance loans are typically** small loans **given to people who do not have access to traditional **banking services,** especially in rural areas.
 
• These loans are used for various purposes such as** starting a small business**, **buying essential goods,** or **paying for education.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **shorter the tenure** of a loan, the higher the **monthly installments,** which can be difficult for borrowers to repay.
 
• Therefore, a** longer tenure** allows for smaller monthly installments, making it** easier for borrowers** to pay back the loan.
 
• It is important to note that microfinance institutions may have their **own policies** regarding loan tenure, which may be different from the regulatory framework.
 
• It is also worth mentioning that microfinance institutions in India are regulated by the **Reserve Bank of India** (RBI) and must comply with its guidelines to operate.
 
• These guidelines are** periodically reviewed** and updated to ensure that microfinance institutions operate in a** fair and transparent manner.**

questions.question: In the Indian Constitution which of the following Articles deals with the right to move to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution deals with the right to move to the Supreme Court for **enforcement of Fundamental rights**.
 
• This article is considered as the **heart and soul** of the Indian Constitution as it provides the citizens with a powerful tool to **safeguard their fundamental rights.**
 
• This article empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the **enforcement of fundamental rights**, which include the right to life and personal liberty, the right to equality, the right against exploitation, the right to freedom of religion, and cultural and educational rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 30 **deals with the** right of minorities **to establish and administer **educational institutions**.

 
 
• This article provides a framework for the protection of** minority rights in the field of education.**
 
 
 
• **Article 33** empowers the Parliament to **restrict or abrogate** the fundamental rights of armed forces, police, intelligence agencies, and other similar organizations.
 
 
• This provision is necessary to maintain the** discipline and effectiveness** of these organizations.
 
 
 
• **Article 31** deals with the right to property, which was removed from the list of fundamental rights by the **44th Amendment Act of 1978.**
 
 
• This amendment was made to ensure that the government could acquire **private property** for public use without any hindrance.

questions.question: Kamsale is the folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kamsale** is a folk dance form from the state of** Karnataka.**
 
• It is primarily performed by the devotees of **Lord Mahadeshwara**, a deity worshipped in the southern parts of Karnataka.
 
• The dance involves the use of **small bronze discs**, called** kamsale**, tied to the ankles of the dancers.
 
• The dancers produce **rhythmic sounds** by striking the kamsale against each other.
 
• Kamsale is considered to be a** sacred dance form** and is performed during religious festivals and fairs in Karnataka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Folk dances of Jharkhand include **Chhau, Jhumar, Santhal, and Karma.**

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a goal of the Five-Year Plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Security.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Five-Year Plans** were a series of economic plans implemented in the** Soviet Union **between **1928 and 1991,** aimed at developing the country's economy.
 
• The goals of the plans were to achieve rapid **industrialization, **increase **agricultural production**, improve **transportation and communication **infrastructure, and develop the country's natural resources.
 
• **Self-reliance** was a key goal of the plans, as the **Soviet Union** wanted to reduce its dependence on foreign imports and technology.
 
• **Equity **was also a** goal**, as the Soviet Union aimed to reduce income inequality and provide basic necessities to all citizens.
 
• **Growth **was a **central goal**, as the plans aimed to increase the country's GDP and improve living standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Security was **not** a stated goal of the Five-Year Plans, although it could be argued that the plans were aimed at strengthening the** Soviet Union's military and geopolitical power.**
 
• Other goals of the plans included **improving education** and **healthcare,** promoting **cultural development**, and advancing **science and technology.**
 
• The Five-Year Plans were** controversial,** as they often involved forced labor, collectivization of agriculture, and suppression of dissent.
 
• Despite their flaws, the plans did lead to significant industrial and technological advancements in the Soviet Union, but also contributed to** environmental degradation and economic inefficiencies.**

questions.question: Ambubachi fair is held every year in which of the following states?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary function of commercial banks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transfer of funds.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transfer of funds** is** not **a primary function of commercial banks, but rather a **secondary function.**
 
• The primary functions of commercial banks include **creating credit, lending loans to the public, and receiving deposits** from the public.
 
• **The creation of credit **involves the bank lending money to **borrowers**, which increases the money supply in the economy.
 
• Lending loans to the public includes providing various types of loans such as **personal loans, home loans, and business loans.**
 
• Receiving deposits from the public involves accepting money from individuals and businesses and holding it in accounts such as **savings accounts, current accounts, and fixed deposit accounts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Transfer of funds is a** secondary function** of commercial banks that involves facilitating the **movement of funds** from one account to another, either within the same bank or between different banks.
 
• The creation of credit is an important function of commercial banks as it helps to **stimulate economic growth **by providing access to capital for businesses and individuals.
 
• Lending loans to the public is a key way in which **commercial banks generate revenue,** by charging interest on the loans they provide.
 
• Receiving deposits from the public is an important function of commercial banks as it provides a source of funds that can be **used for lending and other activities.**

questions.question: Which biosphere was declared as India's 16th Biosphere Reserve in 2009, noted for the conservation of Red Fox, Blue Rock Pigeon, and Lammergeier?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cold Desert.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cold Desert** was declared as India's **16th Biosphere Reserve** in **2009.**
 
• The **Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve** is located in the state of** Himachal Pradesh** and covers an area of **7,770 square kilometers.**
 
• The reserve is home to several endangered species including the **Red Fox, Blue Rock Pigeon, and Lammergeier **(also known as Bearded Vulture).
 
• The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve is also known for its unique landscape, with **cold deserts, alpine meadows, and high-altitude lakes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve** is located in the state of** Andhra Pradesh** and is known for its rich biodiversity.

 
 
• The area is drained by the **Penneru River's tributaries.**
 
 
 
• **Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve **is located in the **southern Western Ghats** and is known for its cultural and ecological significance.
 
 
• 2,000 different types of **medicinal plants **call it home, at least 50 of which are rare and endangered species.
 
 
 
• The **Dehang Debang Biosphere Reserve** is located in the state of **Arunachal Pradesh **and is known for its diverse flora and fauna.
 
 
• Dehang-Debang was established in **1998 **as a biosphere reserve.

questions.question: What is the basic difference in the aggregates at market price and factor cost?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net indirect taxes.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The basic difference in the aggregates at **market price and factor cost **is net indirect taxes.
 
• The taxes that a nation's government levies on the** creation and sale of products **and services are known as indirect taxes.
 
• One such tax is the **GST** (Goods and Services Tax).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Depreciation: **

 
 
• It is the decrease in the value of an asset over time due to **wear and tear, obsolescence,** or other factors.
 
• It is considered in the calculation of **national income **at **factor cost,** but not at market price.
 
 
 
• **Indirect taxes:**
 
 
• These are taxes levied on **goods and services** rather than on income or profits.
 
• Examples include **GST, excise duty, customs duty,** etc.
 
• They are included in the calculation of national income at **market price**, but not at factor cost.
 
 
 
• **Direct taxes:**
 
 
• These are taxes levied on the **income or profits **of individuals or companies.
 
• Examples include** income tax, corporate tax**, etc.
 
• They are not considered in the calculation of **national income **at either market price or factor cost.

• **Ibn Battuta** was a **Moroccan traveler and scholar **who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. 

 
 
• Ibn Battuta observed that the land's soil was very fruitful, enabling farmers to cultivate the two crops of **Rabi and Kharif **each year.
 
 
 
• The most well-known piece by** Ziauddin Barani** is **"Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi."**
 
 
• He placed a strong emphasis on using primary **materials and historical authenticity.**
